html:
Gustav I, called Gustav Vasa, led Sweden out of the Kalmar Union and ruled it as king from 1523 to 1560. He is seen as the founder of the modern Swedish state.

After the Stockholm Bloodbath he raised a revolt in Dalarna, and he was elected king on 6 June 1523, now Sweden's national day. Short of money and fighting the power of the bishops, he broke with Rome from 1527, seized church lands and brought in the Lutheran faith. The Bible was printed in Swedish in 1541.

He built a strong central state with a standing army and an efficient tax system, and in 1544 made the crown hereditary in his family. His sons and grandson, Gustavus Adolphus, made Sweden a great power. The Vasaloppet ski race retraces his escape through Dalarna. See Sweden.
sum: Gustav I, called Gustav Vasa, led Sweden out of the Kalmar Union and ruled it as king from 1523 to 1560. He is seen as the founder of the modern Swedish state.
